import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 109

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture109

open SimpleGraph
/--
WOWII [Conjecture 109](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$, the independence number $\alpha(G)$ was
conjectured to satisfy
$\alpha(G) \le \lfloor (\mathrm{residue}(G) + 2 \cdot b(G)) / 3 \rfloor$, where
$\mathrm{residue}(G)$ is the Havel--Hakimi residue and $b(G)$ is the size of a
largest induced bipartite subgraph.

This is false. A connected graph on 21 vertices has an independent set of size
15, residue 8, and no induced bipartite subgraph with more than 18 vertices, so
the conjectured right-hand side is at most 14.

A smaller counterexample is the connected 13-vertex graph
$\overline K_7 \vee (K_3 \sqcup K_3)$. It has independence number $7$, residue
$2$, and largest induced bipartite subgraph size $9$, so its conjectured
right-hand side is $6$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/DomTheDeveloper/formal-conjectures/blob/cf59008ef1cd432bf9803275dcf5d62ab1f094a3/FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture109.lean",
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/chelokot/wowii-109-counterexample/blob/543a66ee78565b553f4ba6dc7fd32b5610557913/lean/GraphConjecture109.lean#L29-L139"]
theorem conjecture109 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (_h : G.Connected),
      (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ ⌊((residue G : ℝ) + 2 * b G) / 3⌋ := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The invariant `b G` is nonneg (cast of a natural number). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ b G := Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- The residue of $K_2$ equals $1$: degree sequence is $[1, 1]$; one Havel-Hakimi
step gives $[0]$, leaving a single zero. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : residue (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) = 1 := by
  unfold residue
  decide +native

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture109

reformulations.difference: Lean assumes `[Nontrivial α]`, whereas the source states the conjecture for simple connected graphs without explicitly excluding the singleton graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectedness already excludes the empty vertex type. For a singleton vertex type, the graph is edgeless and its independence number, residue, and bipartite number are all 1, so the inequality is 1 ≤ floor((1 + 2)/3) = 1. Thus the universal statement with Nontrivial is equivalent to the statement without it, and their negative answers are equivalent as well. Proved this universal-statement equivalence as Review109.nontrivial_restriction_iff in /workspace/review/singleton.lean, without using the conjecture theorem.

review.notes:
The theorem and both sanity checks are faithful. Checked finite bounds and nonempty witness sets for both supremum-based invariants, Havel–Hakimi termination and zero cases, answer polarity and quantifier scope, and the floor/coercion arithmetic. Lean tests covered empty and singleton graphs, K₂, and small complete and edgeless graphs.

The cited standalone proof compiled against this checkout after namespace renaming, establishing the 13-vertex counterexample with independence number 7, residue 2, and bipartite number 9. Its axioms contain no sorryAx, but include the expected native-decision compiler axioms. Also independently checked a 21-vertex witness for the docstring's numerical claims. These support answer(False) and research solved; the archived original list's O label comes from content last modified in 2020 and does not undermine the verified disproof.

The live source timed out, so archived copies were used. The formal-conjectures-fork proof citation was not inspected, to avoid repository consultation; the separate standalone Lean proof was verified.
